name: Bolshevism
summary: The revolutionary Marxist current led by Lenin that formed in 1903 around a centralised, disciplined vanguard party. It aims to seize power through insurrection, establish a dictatorship of the proletariat through soviets, expropriate capital and plan the economy, and spread revolution internationally, while defending national self-determination and separating religion from the state.
scope: The Lenin-era Bolshevik revolutionary current and its government, 1903–1924, following the Columbia Encyclopedia’s account through the consolidation of its dictatorship (s10), Williams’s account of Lenin and competing Bolshevik tendencies (s9), and Corney’s ideological account (s11). Lenin’s party-building writings are defining texts in s11. The profile retains the earlier audit’s Lenin-era subject rather than importing later Stalinist policies; sustained governing practice takes precedence over aspirational doctrine.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Russell’s Part II, chapter VI records the creation of a large conscript army to defend the regime.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Constitution article 3(e) confirms transfer of all banks to the Soviet Republic; the 1919 programme records their consolidation around the State Bank.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: The State and Revolution, chapter V calls for overcoming subordination to the division of labor, including the opposition between mental and physical work.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The November 1917 decree abolishes all estates, noble ranks, hereditary titles and their associated privileges and legal restrictions.

abolish-income-tax.rationale: Section 22 specifically advocates progressive income and property taxation during the transition.

abolish-ip.rationale: The 1917 and 1919 decrees nationalized intellectual rights and displaced private patents. The NEP patent reform initiated under Lenin restored exclusive, licensable patent rights in September 1924, a policy retained for the rest of NEP.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Goldman pp. 51–57 records the government retaining civil registration and monogamy against proposals for immediate abolition. The enacted code preserved legal marriage during the transition.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Section 21 explicitly proposes expanding non-cash transactions as preparation for abolishing money.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Russell’s Part I, chapters V and VII records an extensive political police apparatus, with spies and prisons functioning as central instruments of government.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Rent-free housing in 1921 was limited to particular workers in public housing; private rentals continued. From 1922 the government explicitly restored regulated rents rather than prohibiting rental housing.

abolish-wage-labour.rationale: State and Revolution says the proletariat must suppress the capitalists to free humanity from wage slavery, and describes a state in which everyone is an employee of one huge syndicate under the Soviets. Wages persisted in the lower phase and under the NEP, so wage labour is an eventual aim and the transitional practice is pay by quantity of labour.

abortion-legal.rationale: The November 1920 decree, paragraphs 1–4, legalizes free abortion in Soviet clinics by qualified physicians while prohibiting lay providers and private profiteering. It is a public-health measure, not the 1918 reform date mistakenly given in the later interview.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Corney’s account connects a sharp break with old institutions to the construction of a modern, technologically advanced society.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: The sources reviewed call for scientific research and public health but do not address funding research to slow biological ageing.

algorithmic-government.rationale: The Lenin-era sources do not address delegating final governmental decisions to artificial intelligence. A local Lenin-corpus search returned no passages for artificial intelligence.

all-land-state-owned.rationale: Constitution article 3(a) abolishes private landholding and explicitly declares the entire land fund national property.

allow-dual-citizenship.rationale: Searched for dual and double citizenship. The 1918 Constitution and the naturalization decree let foreign workers acquire Russian citizenship by simple procedure and do not mention renouncing other citizenship, which is silence.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: No position on animal sentience and the moral standing of animal suffering was found in the reviewed agricultural and conservation materials.

animal-use-humane.rationale: The agricultural and hunting materials do not state a moral condition of humane treatment for killing animals for food.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: The cited nationalities chapter supports secession but does not define the continuing legal status of annexed territory as unlawful occupation.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Collective accounting of production and labor does not by itself settle a general right to untraceable payments.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: The defining account dates Bolshevism’s formation to 1903 but supplies no position on antifascism as a founding value; historical silence is not a mixed position.

apologise-for-past-wrongs.rationale: Crouch reports Bolshevik policy aimed to make amends for the crimes of tsarism against national minorities, and the November 1917 declaration to the Muslims of Russia and the East says their mosques were destroyed and their customs trampled by the tsars and oppressors of Russia and promises rights in reparation. That is public condemnation and amends by the successor state, not a formal apology, so the answer is +1 with low confidence.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The text defends religious freedom but does not address apostasy law; general freedom of religion is insufficient under the current rules.

arbitrator-settles-disputes.rationale: Searched for arbitration, the League of Nations and the Hague. The 1919 programme and Bukharin call the League a capitalist instrument of exploitation, and Bukharin criticises compulsory labour arbitration; no source speaks of binding international arbitration of disputes between countries.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Supporting national liberation or international revolution does not establish a general policy of arming insurgents against any government considered hostile.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The text’s requirement of mass links and a disciplined party is not a documented split over the ability of a small armed group to create revolution.

armed-resistance-to-occupation.rationale: At the Second Comintern Congress Lenin carried the line that communists must support the national-revolutionary movement in backward and colonial countries, and the March 1920 draft calls for direct, unqualified support of all insurrections and revolutionary movements of colonial peoples; Baku in 1920 called for a 'holy war' against imperialism. This supports armed resistance to foreign rule, though the sources speak of colonial rule more than military occupation by name.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Equality of nations and opposition to national privilege do not answer the specific question of immigrants replacing their original culture.

assisted-dying.rationale: No position on medical assistance to dying terminally ill adults was found in the reviewed health and family sources.

automate-paid-work.rationale: The ABC of Communism, chapter III section 22, links mechanization and rising productivity to a continually shorter working day and more time for cultural development.

automation-leaves-most-without-work.rationale: The sources reviewed do not predict automation leaving most people without work. Industrial modernization and the programme’s analysis of capitalist unemployment do not establish that specific prediction.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: The NEP stabilization record shows efforts to reduce deficits and replace inflationary Treasury issuance. It does not establish a position on deficit spending specifically as economic stimulus.

ban-cartels.rationale: The analysis of monopoly as an outcome of capitalism does not establish whether cartels should be prohibited.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Church-state separation does not settle the legal status of cattle slaughter; the earlier answer inferred a specific policy from secularism.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Suppression of Mensheviks does not establish a general policy of banning parties for seeking to abolish the constitutional order.

ban-interest.rationale: The loan decree explicitly preserves savings-bank deposits and the interest paid on them; it does not outlaw lending interest generally.

ban-patents-on-life.rationale: The programme does not address patents on living organisms. The local Lenin-corpus patent leads concern industrial monopoly rather than living organisms.

ban-spanking.rationale: The guardianship and education provisions do not settle a legal prohibition on parental spanking.

basic-income.rationale: Distribution according to labor in the lower phase and according to need later does not directly decide a contemporary unconditional cash income paid by the state.

bound-labor.rationale: The agrarian revolution broke up landlords’ estates and redistributed land to peasant cultivators. The Bolshevik agrarian programme also provided for peasants to migrate from land-short regions to other parts of the country.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Opposition to religious discrimination in state affairs does not settle consumers’ economic boycotts of minority-owned shops.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Combining executive and legislative functions does not by itself decide whether raising revenue or spending requires a representative body’s consent.

build-apartments-freely.rationale: The housing sources address nationalization of large properties, rent and housing allocation. The legal freedom to build apartments on residential land is a separate question they do not settle.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: The defining organizational account makes the disciplined revolutionary party indispensable to leadership, rather than a dispensable intermediary between an individual leader and the people.

capital-controls.rationale: State licensing of foreign trade in goods and particular concessions does not by itself establish a comprehensive policy on capital transfers in both directions.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The introduction explicitly presents capitalism’s collapse and transition to a higher economic system as inevitable.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The programme’s introduction calls imperialist wars for markets, investment and world domination an inevitable consequence of finance capital.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The introduction states that capitalist concentration and socialization of labor create the material possibility of communist production.

central-bank-independence.rationale: The NEP monetary history documents close coordination between the Finance Commissariat, the State Bank and the party leadership, but the passages reviewed do not establish the Bank’s legal decision-making independence.

central-planning.rationale: Section 15 treats a single economic plan as the means of using productive resources efficiently, and section 19 promises national distribution with minimum expenditure of labor.

change-traditions-that-no-longer-suit.rationale: Searched the library for tradition and custom in the decrees and Lenin's youth speech. Bolshevik policy broke with old customs by state decree and party, not by deciding which traditions the living keep; no explicit statement.

character-from-environment.rationale: The analysis of socialist consciousness and worker organization does not establish a general account of how human character is formed.

church-by-bishops.rationale: The text demands independent religious associations but takes no side on episcopal governance of a church.

citizens-assembly.rationale: The constitutional soviets and village meetings are elected or open to eligible electors, not randomly selected assemblies; the sources do not state a position on adding the latter.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Constitution article 20 gives specified foreign workers and peasants political rights and permits their naturalization without formalities; citizenship is not confined to descent from citizens.

civil-disobedience-accept-penalty.rationale: Searched for civil disobedience and accepting penalties or punishment. Only a trade-union article on Russia in the 1990s mentions civil disobedience; no Bolshevik source.

civil-marriage.rationale: Family Code section 52 recognizes marriage registered in the civil registry as the form creating marital rights and obligations; it preserves prior religious marriages under the transitional exception.

civilians-legitimate-targets.rationale: Searched the library and corpus for civilian population, bombardment, terror of the enemy population and hostages. Nothing states a rule on targeting enemy civilians; the Kellogg hostage-taking is domestic repression.

civilizational-union.rationale: An international workers’ alliance does not settle whether countries sharing a civilization should also form a political union.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Opposition to national oppression is not an explicit discussion of a civilizing justification for colonial tutelage.

class-collaboration.rationale: The introductory principles require an independent proletarian party against bourgeois parties and identify their class interests as irreconcilable.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The introductory account explains social revolution through sharpening class contradictions, growing class organization and struggle against exploitation.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: The ABC of Communism, chapter IX section 75, says bourgeois ideology and class habits survive expropriation and require continued struggle; the transition does not immediately abolish social antagonism.

clerical-rule.rationale: Section 13 records the disestablishment of religion from state authority, incompatible with supreme political authority vested in religious scholars.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Opposing national privilege does not directly settle every territorial claim based on a co-ethnic population.

collective-bargaining.rationale: The June 1918 instructions require unions to negotiate wage and working-condition agreements with employers, with compulsory registration and a final decision by the labor commissariat if negotiations fail.

collective-defense.rationale: Criticism of imperialist alliances does not reject all treaty promises of mutual military assistance.

collective-farming.rationale: Section 16 calls for state farms, collective cultivation and voluntary agricultural communes as the route to large-scale socialist agriculture.

colonial-socialism-democratic-stage.rationale: The 1920 colonial report explicitly rejects an inevitable capitalist stage and allows colonial societies to move through soviet organization toward communism with help from advanced-country workers. It does not require a separate bourgeois-democratic regime first.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: The Decree on Peace proclaimed the immediate and unconditional annulment of the secret treaties of the tsarist and Provisional governments that secured annexations and privileges, and the Council of People's Commissars declared these treaties not binding on the Russian people; the Third Congress of Soviets endorsed withdrawal from Persia and self-determination for Armenia. These are treaties of imperial partition repudiated for lacking the peoples' consent, though the decree speaks of Russia's own wartime secret treaties, not colonial-era treaties generally.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Section 9 rejects privileges for the oppressing nation and recognizes dependent nations’ right to separation rather than government for the metropole’s benefit.

communal-electorates.rationale: Separating church and state does not directly settle the design of separate religious electoral rolls.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The programme’s account of class struggle does not explicitly settle whether struggle between peoples is the principal engine of human progress.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Russell’s Part I, chapter V describes central party control and governing presidia exercising power beyond the implementation of local assembly instructions.

conscription.rationale: Constitution article 19 institutes general compulsory military service with differentiated duties by class; Russell records the conscript army in operation.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Russell’s Part I, chapter V records elections managed to preserve Communist rule even though free elections would not have given it a majority.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The January 1918 dissolution decree rejects the elected Constituent Assembly’s competing authority; the constitution was instead adopted through the soviet congress system.

constitution-recognises-indigenous-natio.rationale: Searched for indigenous, aboriginal and natives. The Declaration of the Rights of Peoples and Constitution article 11 recognise peoples and national regions, but no source names indigenous peoples or recognises them as nations.

constitutional-jury-trial.rationale: The Bolsheviks replaced the old court system with people’s courts staffed by judges chosen by workers and with revolutionary tribunals. The new system did not guarantee trial by jury.

cooperative-communities.rationale: The ABC, chapter III section 19, organizes society into an integrated large-scale cooperative economy under an overall production plan, rather than autonomous small communities.

corporate-influence.rationale: The programme’s class analysis does not establish a specific position on corporate lobbying.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: The June 1918 instructions give recognized unions a formal role in wage agreements and submit agreements or unresolved disputes to the labor commissariat for binding approval.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: The sources document measures to repair national and religious oppression in former imperial territories. The evidence reviewed does not establish a separate policy framed around redress for historical racial injustice.

country-wealth-only-from-land.rationale: The ABC of Communism, chapters I–II, derives new commodity value and capitalist wealth from labor and production rather than land alone.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Rejection of liberal parliamentarism does not settle which checks a liberal democracy should place on its national majority.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Secular education does not by itself settle the specific proposal to teach creationism alongside evolution in science classes.

criminalize-genocide-denial.rationale: Searched for genocide in the library. Only 20th-century Ukrainian-famine controversies appear in later scholarship; the Lenin-era scope contains no source on genocide denial.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Healey records 1922 decriminalization in the Russian, Ukrainian and Belorussian republics while sodomy remained a crime in Georgia, Azerbaijan and Central Asian republics. The Lenin-era legal record is divided geographically.

culture-before-state.rationale: The scholarly account describes revolutionary cultural transformation after seizure of power, but does not prescribe a general sequence of national cultural renewal and state-building.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: The nationality programme opposes legal discrimination and protects minority language use. It does not state that cultures are equal on every measure.

death-penalty.rationale: Russell’s Part I, chapter V records thousands of executions by the Extraordinary Commission, while noting a subsequent nominal restriction whose practical effect he could not confirm.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: The early universal protection programme was never implemented in full; the later NEP insurance scheme covered wage workers but excluded self-employed peasants and artisans. This does not establish a guarantee of a decent standard for everyone.

decide-locally.rationale: Russell’s Part I, chapter V describes government pressure over soviet executives and village representatives’ inability to reach higher soviets, with actual power held by the Communist Party.

defeat-communism.rationale: The programme’s introduction explicitly makes communist revolution the party’s goal and calls for international solidarity to secure it.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: The Columbia defining entry explicitly says the Bolsheviks hoped for Russia’s defeat in the imperialist war and sought to turn it into an international civil war.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: The religious and military programmes do not state a religious duty incumbent on every Muslim under foreign invasion.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Section 9 explicitly calls for abolition of national privileges and equality of nations, opposing formal submission of weaker nations to stronger ones.

delink-world-market.rationale: The adopted NEP and actual mixed ventures seek economic relations with capitalist countries rather than terminating them; the policy explicitly uses these relations for recovery.

democracy-becomes-oligarchy.rationale: The ABC treats capitalist parliamentary democracy as minority class rule while affirming the possibility of workers’ rule through soviets. It does not affirm inevitable oligarchy in every democracy.

democracy-best.rationale: Russell’s Part I, chapter V records managed elections and the exclusion of independent campaigning to maintain Communist power despite the absence of an electoral majority.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Sections 1–3 explicitly deny that formal electoral and political procedures suffice for democracy when productive property and material political access remain unequal.

democracy-needs-political-clash.rationale: Searched for opposition, clash of views and criticism. Bolshevik sources defend open criticism within the party and soviets yet also ban factions and rival parties; no statement that democracy needs a clash of opposing positions.

democratic-peace.rationale: The analysis of economic causes of war does not by itself settle whether spreading democracy brings peace.

dense-cities.rationale: The housing and health sources do not compare urban density and suburban greenhouse-gas emissions.

destroy-worshipped-objects.rationale: The early Soviet government returned Islamic sacred objects seized under tsarism, including a venerated Quran given to a Muslim congress in 1917. The government preserved and returned these objects of religious reverence.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Section 2 records class-based deprivation of political rights and suppression of the former exploiters in the Soviet state.

direct-action.rationale: The defining account records both revolutionary insurrection and tactical participation in parliamentary institutions; this does not establish that direct action must replace electoral politics altogether.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The 1918 Constitution places supreme authority in a congress and its elected central executive committee, with the latter forming the government. The executive authority derives from soviet delegates rather than a direct national popular election.

direct-votes.rationale: The Constitution permits village electors to decide local administrative questions directly but does not settle a general requirement that citizens vote directly on major laws.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: The nationalities chapter recognizes nations’ right to a state, but does not prescribe a plebiscite to resolve every disputed territory.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Goldman reports the early legal reforms giving women independent control of their earnings and property, and equal opportunities in work and education rather than legal confinement to a distinct public role.

distribute-by-need.rationale: The State and Revolution, chapter V explicitly makes distribution according to each person’s needs the higher phase of communist society.

distribution-by-process.rationale: The chapter’s critique of equal labor shares concerns distribution within a communist society, not the general contrast between justice by acquisition history and justice by equality.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: A commitment to equality and solidarity across nationalities does not state the effect of ethnic diversity on social cohesion.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The ABC of Communism, chapter XI, explicitly denies supernatural causation of social development and treats the idea of God as a historical human creation.

divinely-chosen-superior-people.rationale: The sources reject supernatural belief but do not discuss this specific doctrine of a divinely chosen superior people.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: The family and welfare sources do not establish an equal right to domestic-violence support services for male victims.

dominated-front.rationale: Lenin’s 1920 reports to the Second Comintern Congress say relations between peoples are determined by the struggle of imperialist nations against the Soviet states, call for union between revolutionary proletarians and the oppressed colonial masses, and promise Soviet help to them. The front is of revolutionary movements and Soviet republics, not only governments.

domination-women-nature.rationale: The emancipation and conservation materials do not link domination of women and domination of nature.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: The reviewed industrial, public-health and conservation materials do not address government action on climate change.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Constitution articles 28 and 35 provide for selection of the central governing organs through congress and executive committee, and article 65(e) disenfranchises the former dynasty rather than recognizing inherited succession.

economic-freedom.rationale: Expropriating property while restricting political freedom does not establish a view about whether lasting political freedom requires economic freedom.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: National equality does not determine whether a national majority should control the economy.

elective-rulers.rationale: Constitution articles 28 and 35 provide for election of the central executive committee and selection of the council of commissars through it, rather than hereditary central government.

elite-replacement.rationale: Opposition to national chauvinism does not address the specific allegation that elites promote immigration to replace a native population.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Russell’s Part I, chapter V records the Cheka’s imprisonment without trial on charges of speculation or counter-revolution during the civil-war regime.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: The indigenization record concerns nationality preferences. It does not settle the statement specifically about abolishing race-based affirmative action.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Class restrictions on political rights do not establish opposition to every constitutionally entrenched bill of rights.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: The reviewed conservation measures do not settle a general priority of environmental protection over individual liberty.

equal-conscription.rationale: The military programme discusses class-based military obligations but does not establish identical draft duties for women and men.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Section 2 explicitly records deprivation of political rights for exploiters, treating class membership as a basis for unequal legal rights.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Section 15 declares eventual equal remuneration for every kind of work as an aim, while allowing higher pay for specialists during the transition.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family Code section 158 uses parental agreement and, failing agreement, court decision on where children live, without establishing an equal-time presumption.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Section 9’s equality of nationalities does not prescribe the ethnic composition of each nation.

ethnicity-statistics.rationale: The 1920 Soviet census asked respondents to identify their nationality and recorded language separately. This made ethnic affiliation a distinct category of official population statistics.

every-country-ready-for-democracy.rationale: Searched for backward countries, ripe for and not ripe. Sources say backward countries can move toward soviet forms and that bourgeois democracy is not a general stage; no statement on every country being ready for democracy.

evolved-behavioural-sex-differences.rationale: The reviewed sources do not present an evolutionary explanation of behavioural differences between women and men.

exclude-trans-women-women-only-spaces.rationale: No position on transgender access to women-only spaces was found in the reviewed family and sexual-policy sources.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: The sources reviewed do not make reduction of human-extinction risk a top public-policy priority.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: The Tax in Kind specifically proposes developing additional oilfields and mines through capitalist concessions when the state lacks the machinery to develop them itself.

expand-nuclear.rationale: The programme and contemporary exposition do not address construction of nuclear power plants. Local Lenin-corpus searches for nuclear power returned no passages; its discussions of atomic physics do not settle energy policy.

experts-over-public.rationale: Section 15 requires technical specialists without political concessions to them; it does not establish their preferred share of policymaking relative to the public.

family-wage.rationale: The labour code’s occupational wage floors do not establish a requirement that one worker’s wage support an entire family.

farm-price-support.rationale: The NEP debate over the spread between farm and industrial prices does not establish a commitment to insulate farmers from swings in prices.

femininity-compatible-with-feminism.rationale: The reviewed emancipation texts do not settle the compatibility of feminine dress and behaviour with feminism.

filial-duty.rationale: Family Code section 163 legally requires children to maintain indigent parents unable to work when public insurance or social security does not already maintain them.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: The reviewed budget and currency measures describe deficit reduction and limits on banknote issuance without establishing a legal ceiling on government borrowing.

flat-income-tax.rationale: The ABC of Communism reports that Soviet Russia levied a graduated income tax, even though collection proved inadequate. That tax did not apply a single percentage rate.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: The earlier answer relied on national doctrine despite acknowledging contrary governing practice; the actual Bolshevik record on secession requires investigation before a replacement answer is justified.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: The land decrees abolish private landownership without a nationality exception, which also prevents foreign private ownership; they allow non-nationality-based use rights.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Constitution articles 20 and 64 grant political rights, including electing and being elected to soviets, to resident foreign workers and non-employing peasants. Eligibility is class-qualified rather than extended to all foreign residents.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: NEP concessions and mixed companies show permitted foreign capital, but do not settle the distinct question of foreign purchase of existing strategic firms.

former-empire-equal-treatment.rationale: Searched for former colonies and empire. Sources discuss the Russian empire's successor states and Finland, with no rule on how a former imperial power should treat lands it once ruled.

four-day-week.rationale: The Code of Labour Laws reported in the 1919 programme sets an eight-hour day as the maximum and 42 hours of uninterrupted weekly rest, which allows a five- or six-day week; the ABC of Communism looks to a continually shorter working day under communism but names no four-day week. The enacted law is at odds with the statement; the aim is silent, so low confidence.

free-basic-services-for-all.rationale: The reviewed programme provides universal free medicine and education, but does not settle free provision of every basic public service irrespective of income.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: NEP allows private and mixed enterprises, but only within a national transition administered and licensed by the Communist government; it does not devolve an unrestricted choice of economic systems to communities.

free-public-college.rationale: Section 12 calls for universities to be open to everyone wishing to study and for material support enabling workers and peasants to attend.

free-trade.rationale: The account of monopoly capitalism does not establish that free trade benefits everyone in the long run or state its opposite.

free-trade-promotes-peace.rationale: Searched for free trade. Lenin and Bukharin treat capitalist competition and capital export as causes of imperialist war, but no source says whether free trade promotes peace.

freedom-is-self-government-of-desire.rationale: Searched for freedom, self-discipline and the realm of freedom. Lenin and Bukharin use Engels's leap from necessity to freedom, which is about conditions of production, not a learned mastery of one's own desires.

future-generations.rationale: The conservation provisions protect particular natural sites; they do not state an obligation to leave the entire Earth undamaged for future generations.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: The interview discusses equality laws and communal services but does not describe a dedicated governmental gender-equality agency.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: The reviewed family law and sexual-policy scholarship do not establish recognition by self-identified gender; later Soviet case discussions do not settle the early Bolshevik position.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: The women’s emancipation sources do not prescribe roughly equal numbers of women and men in every public body.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The sources criticize socially imposed roles and domestic labour without establishing that gender is primarily a social construct.

generational-constitutional-review.rationale: The Constitution assigns amendments to the central congress but does not prescribe periodic opportunities for each generation to revise it.

gm-crops.rationale: The agricultural programme addresses breeding and mechanization, not genetically engineered crops for sustainability.

god-not-male.rationale: The religious chapters reject belief in God but do not address gendered descriptions of God.

government-encourage-intercultural-conta.rationale: Searched for contact between nations and assimilation. Soviet policy promoted separate national cultures through indigenisation and also internationalism of workers, with no statement that governments should encourage contact between cultural groups.

government-nudges.rationale: Searched the library and corpus for nudging and incentive policy. Nothing on gentle steering of choices as against commands.

gradual-change.rationale: Corney’s defining entry describes Bolshevism as demanding a sharp and violent break with the past, rather than reform in small steps.

harm-principle.rationale: The earlier answer treated suppression of class enemies as necessarily exceeding prevention of harm; the cited programme does not settle that philosophical boundary.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Party control of the Red Army does not decide whether the head of state should exercise effective military command.

head-of-state-dissolves-parliament.rationale: The collective Bolshevik dissolution of the Constituent Assembly does not establish a constitutional power for an individual head of state to dissolve parliament.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Opposition to national privilege does not answer the empirical question of genetic causes of average racial-group differences in ability.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: The reviewed reproductive history discusses individual scientists’ eugenic proposals, not an adopted Bolshevik policy discouraging reproduction by people with inherited disabilities.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: The nationalities chapter does not discuss a nation’s spiritual bond to ancestral land.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Section 16 records the complete abolition of private ownership of land, including the land cultivated by individual farmers.

human-caused-global-warming.rationale: The reviewed environmental and scientific sources do not establish a position on human-caused global warming.

human-decline-since-golden-age.rationale: Searched the library and Bukharin's Historical Materialism and ABC for golden age, degeneration and progress of humanity. Sources praise primitive communism and discuss degeneration of ruling classes or of the proletarian leadership, but none says humanity as a whole has declined since a golden age.

human-enhancement.rationale: The sources reviewed do not address adults using technology to enhance themselves; support for scientific and industrial development does not settle this liberty claim.

humans-entitled-to-use-animals.rationale: The ABC, chapter III section 19, expressly includes sheep, horses and cattle among society’s means of production, prescribing their collective use in communist production.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: The chapter’s defense of national equality does not address a language-learning requirement for immigrants.

immigration-favours-shared-culture.rationale: Searched for immigration with culture, language or assimilation. Hits concern assimilation of communist doctrine and of backward masses; no immigration criterion by culture.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The State and Revolution, chapter V distributes consumption shares by work performed while excluding private ownership of productive capital.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: National self-determination alongside class struggle does not establish that political independence means little without economic transformation.

independent-unions.rationale: Ashwin and Clarke describe the 1922 party requirement that union leaders be experienced party members and the unions’ strict subordination to party direction, despite limited scope to defend workers against managers.

indigenous-internal-justice.rationale: The 1920–1922 state authorizes local sharia adjudication in parts of Central Asia and the Caucasus, subject to prohibited punishments and retrial in Soviet courts. This is qualified recognition of internal customary-religious justice.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Early indigenization included removing some colonists and supporting local institutions. The cited account does not establish who had continuing legal authority over traditional land as a distinct jurisdiction.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: The early indigenization programme advanced local peoples into state leadership and gave them preference in employment over Russians in former imperial territories.

indirect-election.rationale: Russell’s Part I, chapter V describes the Moscow Soviet selecting an executive committee which in turn selected the governing presidium.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: The 1919 programme and the enacted insurance law set up complete social insurance for all toilers, with unemployment insurance paid by employers and the state and managed by the insured with the trade unions; the Soviet system of state-run insurance and pensions is the opposite of replacing public pensions with privately managed individual accounts.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Section 9 recognizes the right of colonies and dependent nations to separate, treating a national collective as a holder of rights.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Corney’s account identifies a technologically advanced industrial society as a Bolshevik aspiration and describes its electrification and modernization campaigns.

industrial-unions.rationale: Section 15 calls for unions to abandon narrow craft organization and become industrial associations embracing all workers in each branch.

informal-organisation.rationale: The defining reference describes a permanent disciplined revolutionary party, incompatible with replacing political organization by loose informal circles.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Section 20 records consolidation of banking in a single national state bank, rather than a system of user-owned mutual credit institutions.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Family Code section 71 explicitly states that difference of religion is not an impediment to marriage.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: The right of national self-determination does not separately answer military intervention to preserve another country’s political system.

islam-incompatible.rationale: The sources address religion and class struggle, not Islam’s compatibility with a defined set of Western values.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Lenin’s 1903 and 1913 writings reject Zionist ideas of a Jewish nation and Jewish national culture, but they do not name Bolshevism as a source here and none discusses a state in Palestine, so the question stays unanswered.

job-guarantee.rationale: The NEP Labour Code restored a labour market and unemployment insurance, but its silence on a right to work does not itself establish a position on a universal employer-of-last-resort guarantee.

keep-public-institutions-small.rationale: Searched for small schools and hospitals and for giganticism. The only hits describe the scale of industry; nothing on the size of schools or hospitals.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: The introductory account says colonial superprofits privilege and bribe an upper stratum of workers in wealthy countries, rather than most workers.

labour-priority-over-capital.rationale: The programme’s introductory principles subordinate owners’ interests to workers’ emancipation and replace private productive capital with social property.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: The ABC of Communism, chapter I sections 8–11, explains commodity value through socially necessary labor and capitalist surplus value through unpaid labor.

land-redistribution.rationale: Russell’s Part I, chapter V records the dispossession of large landowners and the transfer of their land to peasants.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Section 16 records the abolition of private landownership while recognizing the continued existence of individual peasant cultivation.

land-value-tax.rationale: The Tax in Kind explains the replacement of grain requisitions with an agricultural levy, and the ABC discusses graduated income and property taxes. Neither establishes a land-value tax replacing most other taxes.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The central judicial and family laws replace religious law, while the government’s 1920–1922 regional system also authorizes sharia courts with restrictions and appeal to Soviet courts. These are differing actions within the same regime.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The cited party-building text does not address obsolescence of the left-right distinction.

legal-duty-to-work.rationale: Rimlinger records the explicit NEP abolition of compulsory labour service, followed by the 1922 Labour Code restricting labour duty to emergencies. This sustained later settlement replaced the earlier general duty to work.

legalize-drugs.rationale: The public-health programme addresses medical supplies and alcohol-related harms. It does not settle the legality of recreational drugs for adults.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Hetherington describes the early Bolshevik authorities choosing not to reintroduce criminal penalties against commercial sex, while creating rehabilitation and alternative-work schemes. This is qualified legal tolerance rather than endorsement of the trade.

limit-campaign-donations.rationale: Searched for campaign funds and election spending. No hits.

limit-growth.rationale: The programme prioritizes productive development, but does not discuss limiting growth specifically to protect the environment.

limit-guns.rationale: Constitution article 3(g) orders complete disarmament of the propertied classes while arming labouring people and creating a Red Army. This is a strict class-based restriction, rather than a universal civilian gun ban.

limit-population.rationale: The reviewed reproductive and economic sources do not advocate actively limiting total population growth.

local-production.rationale: The planning programme discusses coordinated transport and large-scale production, but does not settle whether most goods should be produced near consumers.

local-veto-new-housing.rationale: Searched the housing studies, decrees and Lenin corpus for local control over building. Housing sources cover rent control and requisitioning; nothing on local residents blocking new housing.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Constitution article 20 permits local soviets to confer citizenship on foreign workers and non-exploiting peasants without formalities, rather than a ten-year residence requirement.

majority-settlement.rationale: The cited nationalities chapter does not address state encouragement of majority settlement in minority regions.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: The welfare and emancipation sources do not state the proposed comparison of programmes for disadvantaged men and women.

mandatory-environmental-reporting.rationale: The reviewed sources do not prescribe corporate environmental-impact reporting.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: ABC chapter IX discusses isolating habitual offenders who still pose a danger, but does not specify a statutory minimum sentence for serious repeat offences.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: The adopted NEP permits private trade and capitalist business under Communist state control; the 1922 congress report describes actual mixed enterprises. This is a transitional policy, not a declaration that mature communism is a market economy.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Sections 15 and 19 favor a single plan and the replacement of trade by organized national distribution as the efficient way to meet needs.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Atheism does not settle whether people dying for the nation should be honored as martyrs; the earlier rationale treated religious wording as decisive without evidence on the practice.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: The cited discussion of religion and the press does not address mass entertainment discouraging political challenge.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The programme locates revolutionary transformation in the development of productive forces, capitalist production relations and sharpening economic class contradictions.

maximum-personal-income.rationale: The November 1917 decree sets a monthly salary limit for people's commissars and orders cuts in excessive salaries of high officials, but it covers pay of officials, was later revised for specialists, and the NEP allowed private incomes. Searched for maximum salary, ceilings and party maximum in the library and corpus; no general cap on personal income.

means-match-ends.rationale: Russell records coercion, repression and compulsory industrial labor as the methods used in building a society publicly promised freedom and eventual voluntary cooperation.

member-state-blocks-federal-overreach.rationale: The 1918 Constitution requires local organs to execute higher soviet decisions, empowers higher bodies to annul local decisions, and assigns territorial competence disputes to the central authorities. It gives the binding decision to the centre rather than a unilateral regional veto.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Section 10 subjects military specialists and commanders to the political guidance and supervision of the working class, denying the army an independent guardianship over politics.

military-organisation-revolutionary-part.rationale: Condition 13 of the Terms of Admission to the Communist International (1920) says that in this period of acute civil war the Communist parties can perform their duty only if organised in a most centralised manner and marked by an iron discipline bordering on military discipline, and condition 4 requires Communist cells in every military unit. Left-Wing Communism calls iron discipline the condition of Bolshevik success. The party is organised on semi-military lines though it is described as democratic centralism.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Rejecting national privilege does not directly answer the specific allegation of a secretly conspiring minority.

minority-language-support.rationale: The early nationalities record restores native languages to schools, administration and publishing, extending beyond an abstract equality promise.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Constitution article 11 permits provinces with distinct nationalities and ways of life to form autonomous provincial unions within the federation.

minority-veto.rationale: Internal party discipline does not settle a constitutional minority veto in government.

mixed-constitution.rationale: A class-based soviet state does not settle the philosophical proposition that the best constitution combines rule by the few and the many.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Constitution articles 1 and 12 institute an explicitly republican sovereign structure, while article 65(e) disenfranchises members of the former reigning dynasty.

money-backed-by-precious-metals.rationale: Sanchez-Sibony documents the government’s adoption of a gold-backed chervonets in 1922 to stabilize currency and foreign payments; this replaces the earlier uncontrolled paper-emission practice.

moral-incentives.rationale: Section 15 combines discipline, initiative and material bonuses, but does not establish moral incentives replacing material rewards as the statement proposes.

more-religion-public.rationale: Corney records Bolshevik campaigns against religious institutions, including persecution of clergy as well as propaganda.

municipal-businesses-mixed-economy.rationale: Searched for municipalisation and local enterprises. Lenin rejected municipalisation of land in favour of nationalisation, and the NEP mixed economy was run by the central state and cooperatives; no policy of local governments running businesses beside private firms.

municipal-property.rationale: Sections 14 and 15 assign productive assets to the Soviet Republic and organize them as one national economic unit, rejecting exclusively local ownership.

nation-first.rationale: The programme’s introductory principles reject defense of national capitalist interests in favor of international revolutionary working-class unity.

national-church-status.rationale: Section 13 records church-state separation rather than privileged legal status for an established national church.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The early Soviet authorities restored local-language schooling and publishing and allowed regional religious courts to operate alongside Soviet courts. This gave minority communities room to run cultural and religious institutions under state oversight.

national-mission.rationale: Kept null: the Comintern programme aims at world revolution by proletarian internationalism, not a special national calling of Russia to spread its government.

national-resource-control.rationale: Constitution article 3(b) declares nationally significant forests, minerals and waters to be national property.

national-self-determination.rationale: The governing record denied independence to Georgia through invasion and occupation in 1921 despite recognizing it in 1920. National self-determination was not upheld for peoples who chose a non-Bolshevik state.

native-born-offices.rationale: Constitution article 20 gives eligible resident foreign workers the political rights of Russian citizens, and article 64 includes the right to be elected to soviets; political office is not reserved to native-born citizens.

nature-as-capital.rationale: The planning and conservation sources do not prescribe valuing whole ecosystems as capital in national accounts.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: The conservation record protects natural monuments for scientific and cultural-historical value; it does not settle value independent of human usefulness.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The introductory principles advocate communism as the replacement for capitalism and the route to ending exploitation.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Russell records the regime’s armed defense by a mass army and its use of executions; its record does not prohibit lethal defense.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The enacted system described in sections 14, 20 and 24 includes public ownership, national banking and labor regulation, extending government far beyond protection against physical violence.

no-business-privileges.rationale: The NEP authorized selected commercial concessions and state contracts. The evidence reviewed does not establish whether political connections were the basis for awarding those privileges.

no-central-bank.rationale: Section 20 records the creation of a single national bank by combining nationalised banks and the State Bank.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Church-state separation does not itself rule out political organization by religious denomination.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: A class account of law does not settle whether legal validity alone creates a moral duty of obedience.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Family Code section 87 makes the wish of either spouse sufficient grounds for divorce, without requiring proof of marital fault.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: The reviewed emancipation texts do not advocate avoiding a fixed definition of women in feminist politics.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Sections 12 and 13 record secular coeducation and the decreed separation of school from church.

no-transition-to-communism.rationale: The State and Revolution, chapter V insists on a distinct political transition and distinguishes lower from higher phases of communist society.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Criticism of religious charity as justification for exploitation does not settle a separate doctrine of privileged people’s duties.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Party leadership of the state does not separately settle a nonpartisan ceremonial head of state.

office-by-exam.rationale: Election of judges does not decide the use of competitive examinations for other public offices.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: The 1918 Constitution prescribes election of local soviets and election of executive committees by soviets, with higher congresses chosen through elected delegates. It organizes public authority through elections rather than selection by lottery.

one-party-rule.rationale: Russell’s Part I, chapter V describes effective power concentrated in the Communist Party, with opposition access to printing and meeting halls suppressed.

one-spouse-at-a-time.rationale: Family Code section 68 prohibits a new marriage while a valid prior marriage continues.

online-anonymity.rationale: The sources reviewed do not address a right to online participation without a disclosed legal identity.

online-participation.rationale: The sources address soviet voting and representation, not a right or option to vote through the internet.

open-borders.rationale: The founding Communist International manifesto reproduced in Postgate’s appendix II calls for wiping out state boundaries and organizing the world as one cooperative commonwealth. It makes this an eventual communist objective.

open-government-data.rationale: Constitution article 34 requires the central executive committee to account for its activity and present reports on general policy and particular questions to the congress. This provides for official reporting, though not unrestricted release of all records.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Decriminalization in some republics does not settle eligibility to serve openly in the armed forces.

opposition-only-legal-channels.rationale: Lenin records that the movement used both legal and illegal organization before taking power, including underground activity under tsarist rule.

organic-representation.rationale: Soviet occupational constituencies and party leadership do not establish a general doctrine that organized social groups should replace political parties.

paid-care-work.rationale: Goldman’s Bolshevik vision replaces unpaid housework with paid communal services; it does not establish that unpaid work remaining within individual homes should itself receive wages.

parents-choose-intersex-surgery.rationale: The reviewed sexual-policy scholarship does not establish parental authority to choose infant sex-assignment surgery.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Russell’s Part I, chapter V records the nominally sovereign All-Russian Soviet reduced to ratifying decisions already taken by the Communist Party.

parliamentary-road-socialism.rationale: The ABC, chapter VIII section 62, rejects obtaining socialism by parliamentary majority and treats a revolutionary workers’ army as necessary to establish and defend proletarian power.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Russell’s Part I, chapters V and VII records the suppression of independent political participation and party control over decisions affecting everyday life.

party-commands-army.rationale: Section 10 requires Communist personnel alongside military commanders and political direction and supervision of the army by the working class.

party-controls-media.rationale: Russell’s Part I, chapter V records an entirely official press and the prohibition of independent daily newspapers.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: The Tenth Congress orders factions dissolved and requires their members to remain at work under party discipline, with expulsion for noncompliance.

party-own-road.rationale: At the 1920 congress Lenin rejects the claim that British communist tactics concern Britain alone and insists that the International debate and determine the correct course.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Goldman’s account of Bolshevik thought identifies men’s economic control and women’s unequal household burden as structural obstacles to women’s independence.

patriotic-education.rationale: The public education programme aims to develop a communist outlook and train workers. It does not specify a distinct duty to teach patriotism.

pay-for-effort.rationale: State and Revolution says the lower phase of communism applies the principle that he who does not work shall not eat and 'an equal amount of products for an equal amount of labour'; in March 1918 Lenin urged piece work and the Taylor system. Pay by the amount of labour contributed is the Bolshevik rule for the transition. Effort is read as labour contributed, not as need or equal shares.

pay-off-national-debt.rationale: The February 1918 loan decree repudiates tsarist and provisional-government borrowing, including all foreign loans, rather than repaying the inherited national debt.

people-in-arms.rationale: Russell’s account records a large conscript army under centralized command; the government did not replace it with the universally self-administering citizen force of its early ideal.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The 1918 Constitution places all power in the soviets of workers and peasants, and the First Decrees abolish estates and ranks; no source rests authority on personal oaths between followers and lords.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The State and Revolution, chapter V makes production common property while describing individuals receiving consumer goods for their own use.

physical-labour-duty.rationale: The programme requires useful labor from those able to work but also recognizes scientific and intellectual work; it does not require everyone to do physical labor.

political-borders-follow-ecosystems.rationale: The national-territorial and conservation sources do not propose drawing political borders along ecosystem boundaries.

political-decisions-consensus.rationale: The 1921 congress adopted binding party resolutions, ordered factional groups dissolved and authorized expulsions; decisions bound dissenters rather than requiring their consent.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The programme’s class account of bourgeois government does not say that most individual politicians prioritize personal interests.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: The text analyzes religious oppression and class struggle without directly addressing politics as a spiritual struggle against evil.

pollution-taxes.rationale: No comparison preferring pollution taxes over environmental regulation was found in the economic or conservation sources.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: The justice and conservation sources do not propose replacing regulatory agencies with pollution-damage lawsuits.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Lenin’s 1915 article judges a United States of Europe under capitalism impossible or reactionary, but it does not name Bolshevism and is not tied to it as a source; no Bolshevism-defining source settles pooling sovereignty.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The ABC explains poverty and unemployment through capitalist relations but does not settle the comparative claim that population growth, rather than unequal distribution, causes poverty.

population-transfer.rationale: The argument against national privilege does not settle expelling a minority judged hostile; the earlier rationale did not document a position on this measure.

positive-liberty.rationale: Section 3 contrasts formal rights with workers’ actual ability to use them and calls for material means that make assembly and the press accessible.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: National-territorial and soviet representation do not establish a guaranteed executive share for every major community in divided societies.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Workplace safety and nature-reserve provisions do not establish a general environmental rule for action before scientific certainty.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: The April 1918 monuments decree orders removal of tsarist monuments lacking artistic or historical value, while allowing those judged valuable to survive.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Prioritizing international class solidarity does not settle whether national cultural heritage should be preserved.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Section 3 argues that printing works, paper and meeting halls controlled by the wealthy prevent workers from actually exercising formally equal freedoms.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Russell records food requisition and suppression of private speculation, which do not establish the specific use of maximum legal food prices. The earlier Wikipedia-based claim needs a decree or a historical account of price-setting.

price-controls-fight-inflation.rationale: The NEP sources describe the scissors crisis as a divergence between industrial and agricultural prices, and distinguish that problem from depreciating currency. Controls aimed at relative prices do not settle whether controls are a good general response to inflation.

price-stability-first.rationale: The chervonets reform defended currency stability in a specific monetary crisis. The primary position of price stability among all economic goals is not established.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Sections 12 and 18 give special priority to workers and poor peasants in access to universities and in political organization.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Section 11 records the abolition of the former courts and their replacement by a uniform people’s court, with judges elected by the toilers and implementing Soviet decrees.

production-for-use.rationale: The mature NEP record reorganizes state enterprises commercially and permits mixed profit-seeking companies. This is a sustained transitional use of profit production rather than its outright replacement in practice.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The introductory account says capitalists’ income is created by the labor of workers compelled to sell their labor power and identifies this relation as exploitation.

prohibit-child-medical-transition.rationale: No position on medical gender transition for children was found in the reviewed family and sexual-policy sources.

promote-democracy-abroad.rationale: The ABC calls for spreading soviet proletarian democracy worldwide and expressly rejects bourgeois parliamentary democracy as the form to pursue.

promote-ethnic-return-migration.rationale: Searched for repatriation and return of ethnic groups to their native countries. Hits concern wartime emigrants and Georgian refugees; no policy of promoting return of foreign-origin peoples.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Bolshevik repression included Cheka executions without trial, including retaliatory shootings in Georgia in 1923; government force was not confined to proceedings before recognized judges.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Maternity protection and infant care do not establish incentives conditional on having additional children.

property-franchise.rationale: Constitution articles 64–65 enfranchise productive workers and exclude employers seeking profit and recipients of unearned property income, the reverse of a property-owner-only franchise.

property-fundamental.rationale: Section 14 records extensive expropriation of productive property, and section 16 the complete abolition of private landownership.

property-sabotage-justified.rationale: Searched for sabotage in the library and corpus. Nearly all hits describe capitalists' or officials' sabotage of Soviet power, not sabotage of property as political action.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Socialization of productive property does not establish a conditional justification of private property by its service to the common good.

proportional-representation.rationale: The Constitution allocates soviet delegates by population, electors and locality; this does not establish a position on proportional allocation of legislative seats among parties.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Constitutional reports from executive bodies to soviets do not establish an individual legal right of access to government records.

public-money-creation.rationale: The Bolshevik government issued Treasury notes and by decree authorized the State Bank to issue gold-backed notes. Both channels of national currency issuance were public institutions.

public-ownership.rationale: Section 14 records that expropriation of the bourgeoisie was largely completed, making industrial ownership a public rather than private institution.

public-service-media.rationale: Russell’s Part I, chapter V records state ownership of printing and a wholly official press, denying independent editorial control.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The cited text supports religious liberty but does not address blasphemy law specifically.

race-based-immigration-restrictions.rationale: The 1918 Constitution grants political rights and citizenship to foreign workers without formalities, gives asylum to those persecuted for political or religious offences, and declares racial or national privileges or restrictions contrary to the fundamental laws; the 1918 naturalization decree lets any alien who resides in Russia apply. No racial test appears. Lenin's 1922 note ordering a stop to illegal immigration targets profiteers and counter-revolutionaries, not a race.

racial-community-economic-control.rationale: Searched for economic autonomy by race or nation and for Black republic and Negro self-determination. No hits in the library or corpus.

racial-franchise.rationale: Constitution article 64 grants the franchise irrespective of nationality, and article 22 explicitly rejects limitations and privileges based on race or nationality.

racial-group-interests.rationale: National and class solidarity do not directly settle whether racial groups should organize to defend distinct political interests.

racial-oppression-before-sexism.rationale: Searched for race oppression, Negro workers and women's equality. Sources treat class as the main line; no ranking of racial oppression over sexism.

racial-pride.rationale: The nationality chapter condemns national prejudice and antisemitism, but does not settle the legitimacy of racial pride as distinct from hostility.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Article 22 of the 1918 Constitution explicitly prohibits racial privileges and restrictions, including the legal disadvantages on which enforced racial segregation depends.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The programme regulates wages and the interview reports early women’s rights, but Goldman’s modern advocacy of a living wage is her own position rather than evidence of a historical Bolshevik minimum-wage requirement.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The ABC of Communism, chapter XI, explicitly rejects supernatural explanations in favor of scientific explanation and calls religious belief incompatible with communism.

recall-officials.rationale: Russell’s Part I, chapter V reports regular recalls of Moscow Soviet members, including for failure to report to their electors.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Russell’s Part I, chapter V reports the use of recall in the Moscow Soviet, although Communist control constrained electoral competition.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Lenin’s 1913 article calls workers’ migration progressive and says only reactionaries shut their eyes to it, but it does not name Bolshevism or discuss quotas, so it is not cited and the question stays unanswered.

refuse-to-join-illegitimate-government.rationale: In March 1917 Lenin praised Chkheidze, a Duma deputy, for refusing to enter the second Provisional Government as 'proletarian policy' and condemned his joining the first as participation in the government of the imperialist war; the Bolsheviks themselves refused to join the Provisional Government. The Bolshevik view was that a government of capitalists is illegitimate for socialists; the statement is broader, so low confidence.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Constitution articles 49(d), 49(f) and 50 assign the central congress and executive committee authority to fix regional competencies and administrative divisions and take additional questions into their jurisdiction.

regional-resource-ownership.rationale: The Decree on Land declares all mineral wealth, forests and waters of national importance the property of the whole people, administered by the state, and the 1918 Constitution unifies state revenue in one general budget; regions are not owners of the resources found on their territory. Autonomous regions are allowed to differ in way of life but no source gives them ownership of resources.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: The 1918 Constitution unifies all state revenue and expenditure in one general budget; the All-Russia Congress or Central Executive Committee decides which taxes go to the central budget and which to local soviets, local soviets may tax only for local needs, and local estimates are approved by higher bodies. Regions do not keep most of what they raise.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Under the sustained NEP settlement the state licensed capitalist concessions through detailed binding agreements, retained command of major industries and supervised mixed companies. Private corporate activity operated under extensive state control.

rehabilitation.rationale: The ABC records ordinary courts using conditional sentences and corrective labour with a rehabilitative aim. Russell separately records punitive incarceration and penal settlements for labour discipline, showing a mixed governing record.

reification.rationale: The ABC of Communism explains that exchanging goods in a commodity economy makes mutual dependence between producers appear as market transactions between their products.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: The religious programme rejects supernatural belief and promotes atheism; it does not prescribe reinterpretation of religious doctrine for modern believers.

religion-from-peoples-character.rationale: The religious programme explains religion through historical social conditions; it does not prescribe a religion expressing each people’s character.

religion-illusion.rationale: The ABC of Communism, chapter XI, presents religious consolation and belief in supernatural forces as products of oppression and ignorance, rather than true remedies for suffering.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: The discussion treats religion as class oppression but does not identify religion as a major cause of women’s oppression.

religions-one-truth.rationale: The attack on religious belief does not examine the claim that all authentic religions express a single underlying spiritual truth; the earlier citation did not address this specific proposition.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: School-church and church-state separation do not decide whether religious clothing should be prohibited in state institutions.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Constitution article 13 separates church from state and permits religious and anti-religious propaganda without privileging one creed; article 65 excludes clergy of religious cults generally from voting.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Crouch documents alternative medical service for religious conscientious objectors from 1918–1919 and later regional religious-law accommodations.

religious-nation.rationale: The text addresses religion’s relation to the state and party, not the criteria defining a national community.

religious-offensive-war.rationale: Searched for holy war, jihad, crusade and religious wars. The Baku call for a holy war was against imperialism and the ABC calls the defence of the republic a holy war; nothing speaks of war to impose a religion's rule.

remove-indigenous-peoples.rationale: The first decrees of Soviet power proclaim the equality and sovereignty of the peoples of Russia, abolition of all national and national-religious privileges and restrictions, and free development of national minorities and ethnic groups. No source proposes removing a people from its land, and the decrees point the other way. Searched the saved library and the marxists corpus for the decree wording; no counter-example found.

remove-other-ethnic-groups-from-country.rationale: The Declaration of the Rights of the Peoples of Russia and the 1918 Constitution abolish all national privileges and restrictions and declare racial or national oppression contrary to the fundamental laws; the Council of People's Commissars made persecution of any nation, and pogroms, criminal. Expelling an ethnic group from the country is the opposite. Searched the saved library and corpus for expulsion and deportation; hits concerned individual opponents, not ethnic groups.

rent-control.rationale: Rents were frozen in Moscow and Petrograd in 1919. The 1922 restoration of rents imposed binding maximum rates on both private and public housing, with criminal sanctions for landlords who exceeded them.

replace-appointed-officials.rationale: Searched the saved library, Lenin 1917-23 and Bukharin 1917-24 for recall and rotation. Sources say all officials are elected and subject to recall at any time and that administrative functions will be performed by each in turn, but they speak of elected, not appointed, officials and give no fixed term.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: The earlier answer relied on Lenin’s ideal of worker-paid officials, but the governing record reviewed so far does not establish representatives’ actual pay relative to average workers.

reserved-seats-excluded-groups.rationale: Searched for reserved seats, quotas and proportional representation. Lenin's 1917 programme asked for proportional representation generally; the Soviet franchise weighted workers, but no reserved seats for historically excluded groups appear.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The sources justify class revolution but do not make violation of a constitution the stated basis of a right of resistance.

resist-oppression-despite-death.rationale: Searched for sacrifice of life, dying for and martyrs. The ABC dedicates the book to martyrs of the party, but no source states a duty to resist oppression at the cost of one's life.

restore-past-order.rationale: Corney’s defining account describes Bolshevism as a militant break with the old order oriented toward a new collectivist society.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Socialism and Religion defends freedom of belief, but the current rules require specific evidence on legal restrictions on religious conversion.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Russell’s Part I, chapters V and VII records coercive industrial discipline and compulsory work as methods of developing production.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The July 1918 Council of People’s Commissars resolution declares persecution of any nation criminal, orders soviets to root out the anti-Semitic movement and puts those conducting pogrom agitation outside the law. It targets agitation that leads to violence against a group, so the position is qualified rather than a general ban on offensive speech.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: The early indigenization record includes removal and resettlement of Russian and Cossack colonists to address imperial settlement and restore local peoples’ position.

restrict-private-adult-pornography-acces.rationale: The reviewed public-health and eyewitness materials discuss prostitution and social conditions, without establishing a prohibition on pornography.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Russell’s Part I, chapter VII records strikes as illegal, even though they sometimes occurred.

restrict-technology-exports-to-rivals.rationale: Searched for export restrictions and the foreign-trade monopoly. The monopoly of foreign trade controlled all trade, not advanced technology to rival countries specifically.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Condemnation of imperialist exploitation does not specify restructuring international economic rules in favor of developing countries.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The role assigned to revolutionary theory and practical experience does not directly settle judging all policies irrespective of ideology.

return-to-foraging.rationale: The ABC, chapter III sections 19 and 22, makes developed large-scale machine production the material basis of the desired society. A return to subsistence hunting and gathering contradicts that specified productive organization.

return-to-pre-conversion-religion.rationale: The religious programme does not advocate restoration of a people’s pre-conversion faith.

revive-national-language.rationale: The chapter addresses national equality and secession, not revival of a dormant national language.
