rich-first.rationale: Social ownership and a national development plan do not establish whether some regions may become wealthy before others.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Section 23 nationalizes capitalist housing and proposes better worker housing, without deciding a statutory right for council tenants to buy.

right-to-secede.rationale: Section 9 recognizes national and colonial separation, not an unrestricted right for any administrative region to secede; the earlier citation did not cover that broader claim.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: National equality does not settle where diaspora populations should seek rights rather than a homeland.

rule-by-example.rationale: Russell’s Part I, chapters V and VII records extensive police surveillance, imprisonment without trial and compulsory industrial labor as methods of government.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: The programme describes repression and ideology without documenting a split over consent being the main basis of ruling-class power.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Criticism of isolated small farming and its cultural backwardness does not settle the statement comparing the moral health of rural and urban life.

sacred-nation.rationale: Internationalist class priorities do not address whether a nation is a sacred transgenerational community.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Church-state separation and materialism do not document the status of the head of state as sacred or nonsacred; the earlier answer did not provide evidence on that office.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Lenin tells the Youth Leagues that proletarian culture is not invented but must be the logical development of the knowledge accumulated under earlier societies, rejecting those who want to start from nothing.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The reviewed family law and sexual-policy scholarship do not establish a general legal entitlement to same-sex marriage during this profile’s period.

say-in-proportion-to-effect.rationale: Searched for directly affected, those concerned and local self-government. Sources support local self-government and soviets but not a principle that influence scales with how much a decision affects a person.

school-vouchers.rationale: The programme calls for free secular education but does not address parents receiving public vouchers for schools of their choice.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: The ABC of Communism, chapter XI, rejects religious explanations as fables and denies divine or supernatural causation, contradicting an error-free divine scripture.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: The religious and women’s emancipation texts do not state this criterion for judging scripture.

second-chamber.rationale: The constitution establishes a hierarchy of soviets and a central executive committee, but does not directly settle a general proposal for a second legislative chamber.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Russell’s Part I, chapter V describes the Extraordinary Commission imprisoning people without trial and executing thousands without proper trial, operating largely independently of government.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Corney identifies the intended new Soviet person with collectivist aspirations rather than selfish pursuit of personal gain.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: The NEP sources describe necessary foreign trade, capital and concessions but do not settle a general ranking of domestic resources over foreign development finance.

separate-church-state.rationale: Section 13 explicitly records the already decreed separation of church and state.

separated-powers.rationale: Constitution article 31 makes the Central Executive Committee the supreme legislative, executive and supervisory body, uniting functions rather than separating them into mutually checking powers.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: The family and sexual-policy sources do not state that biological sex itself is socially constructed.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Goldman pp. 51–53 describes the 1918 Code eliminating husbands’ authority over wives and establishing spouses’ equal independence and obligations.

shut-down-tax-havens.rationale: Searched for tax haven, offshore and capital flight. Lenin and Bukharin discuss the export of capital as an imperialist feature, with no mention of tax havens.

single-common-good.rationale: A class-based state and a future classless society do not settle the statement’s contrast between a reasoned common good and political bargaining.

single-official-language.rationale: The cited self-determination chapter does not address a sole compulsory language of public life; the prior answer requires a text specifically on language policy.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Support for national autonomy does not settle a general rule that all administrative regions inhabited by one people must merge.

slavery-reparations.rationale: Searched for reparation, indemnity and compensation to descendants of slaves. Hits are about war indemnities and preparations; nothing on slavery reparations.

small-step-social-reform.rationale: Corney’s defining account describes Bolshevism as a sharp and irrevocable revolutionary break with the inherited order.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Section 11 records abolition of the former courts and replacement by a new Soviet judicial structure; the revolutionary state did not simply retain the old governing institutions.

social-market-economy.rationale: Under the sustained NEP turn the government permits private trade and mixed enterprises while retaining public industry and social provision. It accepts this combination provisionally rather than as the final communist system.

socialism-needs-revolutionary-war.rationale: State and Revolution teaches that the proletariat's state replaces the bourgeois one only by violent revolution, and the ABC of Communism says the imperialist war is ending in a civil war whose outcome will be victory of the proletariat and calls the war against Russia's enemies a holy war of deliverance. Lenin also accepted revolutionary wars if the interests of socialism demanded. 'Revolutionary war' is read here as violent revolution and civil war; the sources do not require a war between states, so +1.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The effective governing power described by Russell lies in the party leadership rather than autonomous working-class voting; the fuller programme’s promise of worker rule does not overturn that record.

socialism-one-country.rationale: The sources reviewed here stress world revolution but do not settle whether lasting socialism in one country necessarily requires foreign socialist revolutions; the earlier sources did not establish the specific necessity.

socialized-care.rationale: Goldman, chapter 1 pp. 2–4, identifies replacing individual household labor with paid communal dining, laundries and childcare as central to the Bolshevik vision of women’s emancipation.

socialized-markets.rationale: The NEP governing record includes private and mixed capitalist firms alongside public industry, rather than making all market enterprises worker-owned.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Revolutionary defeatism in an imperialist war does not establish that soldiers should refuse to fight in all wars between states.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Class dictatorship is not a stated doctrine of a personal sovereign standing above law.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: The explanation of financial imperialism does not call for cancellation of poor countries’ foreign debts; Russian repudiation alone would not establish that general policy.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Lenin describes state-capitalist elements within a mixed transitional economy; this does not settle the assertion that the Soviet Union as a whole was a state-capitalist society.

space-expansion.rationale: The Lenin-era programme and contemporary exposition do not make human expansion into space a central goal.

spiritual-nature.rationale: A materialist outlook and criticism of religion do not settle the general proposition that politics should serve people’s spiritual needs.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: The programme’s arming of workers and the creation of a Red Army do not clarify whether arms may be held only by state forces; hunting permissions are a separate issue.

state-as-business.rationale: The programme presents public economic administration and a class state, but does not settle a general proposition about running government on business principles.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Section 2 states that every state is necessarily a class state while classes exist, and section 1 calls the bourgeois state a machine for exploitation and suppression.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Section 15 requires a unified national economic plan and the central concentration of productive resources, while section 16 calls for state investment in agricultural improvement.

state-finances-worker-businesses.rationale: Section 15 proposes financial assistance to producer cooperatives and artisan associations as they combine into larger productive units.

state-harmful.rationale: The ABC of Communism, chapter III, expressly aims at disappearance of the state after classes vanish, while defending a coercive transitional state. The statement does not demand immediate abolition.

state-laws-apply-online.rationale: The sources reviewed do not address applying state law on the internet; a theory of state power does not settle that specific technological setting.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Sections 12 and 13 make schools vehicles of communist education and call for wide scientific and anti-religious propaganda using the new educational order.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Corney identifies hostile encirclement and civil war as formative conditions of Bolshevik coercive rule; Russell records the mass army and political police built under that pressure.

state-supports-good-ways-of-life.rationale: The ABC, chapter X section 78, directs the new school to instil a proletarian outlook and prepare children for communist social relations. The state is assigned an active role in forming preferred ways of life.

strong-leader.rationale: The defining sources describe a centralized revolutionary party, not a proposal that an individual leader bypass political gridlock.

students-direct-own-learning.rationale: The ABC, chapter X section 80, prescribes a common compulsory programme of general and technical education; individual specialization is allowed only without detriment to that common curriculum.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Separation from the state and opposition to religion do not establish support for a state-controlled church.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Russell’s Part I, chapter V records suppression of independent newspapers and campaigning, and chapter VII records prolonged imprisonment of political opponents without trial.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Russell records extensive secret-police surveillance and informants. His account does not isolate a policy of surveillance specifically to prevent terrorism.

tax-holding-cash.rationale: The account describes depreciation from Treasury note issuance as an implicit tax. It does not establish support for a tax on cash balances when prices are stable.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Expropriation of productive property does not settle the separate question of heavily taxing large inheritances.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Section 22 calls for a progressive income and property tax during the transition, replacing initial levies imposed on capitalists.

taxation-theft.rationale: The enacted loan, revenue and ownership decrees raise and redistribute public resources; the programme explicitly authorizes taxation instead of treating it as intrinsically illegitimate.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The ABC expects enormous benefits from improved machinery alongside transformed social relations; it does not say technological progress itself solves most human problems.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Corney describes Bolshevik modernization as a sharp break with the past, rather than modernization combined with restoration of ancestral values.

term-limits.rationale: The Constitution sets short terms for local soviet deputies but does not limit the number of terms a politician may serve.

territorial-expansion.rationale: National equality does not establish a position on territorial expansion by a strong state; the wartime governing record also requires examination.

torture-always-illegal.rationale: Kellogg documents recurrent Cheka torture and official beatings in 1918–1919, rather than an isolated offence, including abuse ordered by military officers. This governing record does not uphold an unconditional prohibition.

total-state.rationale: Control of production and communist education do not establish state direction of every area of life.

trade-surplus.rationale: The NEP monetary reform set exports exceeding imports by 10–15 percent as a condition for replacing the old currency with the chervonets. This was a specific stabilization objective.

traditional-family.rationale: Goldman’s defining account says the Bolshevik project sought the withering away of the family as an economic unit through socialized domestic services and women’s independent earnings.

treaties-binding.rationale: The constitutional distribution of treaty powers does not specify a requirement for a constituent nation’s consent before changing a domestic treaty.

troops-home-from-abroad.rationale: The Decree on Peace and the early Soviet declarations rejected annexations and occupations, and the Council of People's Commissars began withdrawing troops from Persia and gave Armenia the right to self-determination in 1917-18. Against this the Red Army later entered Georgia (1921) and Persia (1920), so the position is a stated principle with contrary practice and is scored with qualification.

turn-back-illegal-migrants.rationale: Searched for illegal crossing and frontier guards. Lenin's November 1922 note orders resolute measures against illegal immigration of Russians and Americans said to be profiteers and counter-revolutionaries, a single order about specific people, not a policy on migrants caught at the border.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: The reviewed record of political secrecy and surveillance does not establish a position on a public right to government-proof encryption.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: The Family Code creates a common civil framework, but the 1920–1922 record also establishes parallel sharia courts and regional accommodations. The actual legal record combines uniform civil law with religious exceptions.

unions-good.rationale: Sections 15 and 24 record unions participating in industrial management, factory inspection and wage-setting, giving workers organized influence within the Soviet system.

unions-run-economy.rationale: The Tenth Congress rejects the Workers’ Opposition demand for economy-wide administration by an all-producers’ congress; the governing party retains direction of economic institutions.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Section 25 requires skilled medical treatment and medicines to be freely accessible to everyone.

universal-morality.rationale: Socialism and Religion attacks religious beliefs but does not state a theory about whether any moral truth holds across all cultures.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: The Constitution does not establish a directly elected presidency or state a position on unlimited presidential reelection.

unpaid-domestic-work-exploitation.rationale: Goldman describes the Bolshevik account of unpaid housework as a burden that kept women economically dependent even after they entered paid employment. Their programme sought to transfer that work to paid workers in public services.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Rejection of religious government does not settle whether failure to apply religious law provides a justification for armed overthrow.

vanguard-party.rationale: The Columbia defining entry identifies a small, disciplined party of professional revolutionaries as Lenin’s distinctive organizational principle.

vote-at-sixteen.rationale: Constitution article 64 normally sets voting eligibility at eighteen, but expressly allows local soviets to lower the age with central approval. It does not establish either a general entitlement at sixteen or an unconditional rejection of that age.

vote-delegation.rationale: Russell describes delegates holding offices in hierarchical soviets, but does not settle whether separate policy-area delegation should be allowed.

wages-fall-to-bare-minimum.rationale: The ABC of Communism, chapter II, acknowledges that real wages rose during capitalist development even as profits rose faster; it does not accept an invariant return to bare subsistence.

war-builds-character.rationale: The economic explanation of imperialist war does not answer whether war strengthens national character.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Sections 1 and 3 describe concentrated capitalist property as the source of domination and the material obstacle to exercising political freedoms.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: International class solidarity does not settle the citizenship qualifications for welfare benefits.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Section 15 calls for small producers to combine into larger units leading to mechanized industry, and section 16 makes large-scale socialist agriculture the eventual aim.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Family Code section 87 expressly permits divorce on either spouse’s request; mutual consent is an alternative ground rather than a requirement.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: An organization’s demand for committed revolutionaries does not settle whether withdrawal from public affairs is a better way of life in general.

women-distinct-values.rationale: The women’s emancipation programme does not state that women are inherently more compassionate.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Goldman, chapter 1 pp. 2–4 and 57–58, explains that Bolsheviks considered capitalism incapable of resolving women’s double burden and regarded socialist economic transformation as necessary.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: The religious programme addresses secularization and atheism, not equal eligibility within every religious office.

women-must-cover.rationale: Church-state separation does not state a position on mandatory female dress.

women-organise-apart-from-men.rationale: Searched for separate women's organisations, Zhenotdel and women with men. The Zhenotdel was a party department, not an independent women's organisation, and no source says women should organise apart from men.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: The family legislation reviewed establishes spouses’ separate property and legal capacity, but does not address equal land rights specifically. Research on land-use rights remains pending.

women-suffrage.rationale: Constitution article 64 expressly gives the same voting and eligibility rights to citizens of both sexes.

work-centre-of-life.rationale: Searched for universal labour service, 'he who does not work shall not eat' and labour as duty. Sources make labour a duty but the ABC also looks to a shorter working day with leisure; none says work is the centre of life.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Under NEP, unemployment assistance depended on registration, need and previous employment, while sickness and disability benefits covered inability to work; compulsory labour itself had been abolished. This replaced wartime universal labour service with employment-related eligibility.

worker-farmer-alliance.rationale: The introduction makes the support of the poorest peasantry part of proletarian rule, and section 18 calls for an organized alliance linking rural laboring strata to urban workers.

worker-ownership.rationale: Section 14 assigns productive assets to the republic as the common property of all toilers, rather than specifying ownership of each business by its own workforce.

workers-anti-imperialist-capitalist-alli.rationale: The 1920 colonial report supports bourgeois-led liberation movements only when genuinely revolutionary and when they permit independent communist organization of exploited people; opposition to foreign domination alone is insufficient.

workers-councils.rationale: The government retained soviets and occupational constituencies, but Russell’s Part I, chapter V found actual authority concentrated in their Communist presidia and the party.

workers-nation.rationale: The introduction rejects social-chauvinism for defending the fatherland’s rapacious interests and instead requires fraternal international proletarian unity.

workers-own-party.rationale: The introductory principles require the proletariat to organize an independent political party opposed to bourgeois parties.

workers-parties-campaign-reforms.rationale: Searched for partial demands, the minimum programme, reforms within capitalism and parliamentary participation. Left-Wing Communism chapter 9 favours electoral compromise with the Labour Party to expose it, and the programme calls the minimum programme achievable only after revolution; neither settles a campaign for reforms within capitalism.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Ashwin and Clarke describe NEP management retaining enterprise authority while unions mediate grievances and remain subordinate to party direction; workers do not independently vote on overall company management.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: The cited imperialism chapter identifies monopoly and financial dependence, but does not establish the specific proposition that wealth transfers keep poor countries poor.

youth-equal-civil-rights.rationale: The 1918 Family Code, sections 190–192, places minors under parental or appointed guardianship until the specified ages of majority. Minors do not hold the same independent civil capacity as adults.

missingStatements.text: In a war between rival great powers, working people should work for their own government's defeat rather than support it.
missingStatements.rationale: The Columbia defining entry explicitly records Bolshevik support for defeat in the imperialist war and its transformation into international civil war.

notes: Lenin-era Bolshevism, 1903–1924. Statements without a stated position in the saved library or the marxists corpus are left null; the next pass takes them up.

aliases.name: Bolshevik
